browser: Google Chrome via CDP; audio decode confirmed separately in --headless=new

does_not_prove: visual design quality, responsive behaviour at other viewports, or accessibility
that a human finds the page usable
proves: the journal UX renders in a real browser at 1440x900 with journal prose, tone chips and provenance footnotes
footnote links resolve to their source anchors
the audio player resolves its source and loads the journal audio at its true duration

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: audio element src was a file:// URI built with Path.as_uri(); a browser blocks file:// media on an http:// page, so the player reported networkState 3 (NO_SOURCE) and never loaded
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: emit a path relative to the page when the audio sits beside it, falling back to a file URI only when out of tree; works under both http:// and file://

defects_found_and_fixed.defect: page header rendered a Python dict repr, {'display_name': 'Embry', 'id': 'embry'}, because dream_packet stores persona as an object and the renderer called str() on it
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: persona_name() reads display_name/id, and still accepts the bare string older receipts carry

false_lead_recorded.cause: document.hidden was true; Chrome defers media decoding in hidden tabs
false_lead_recorded.how_it_was_excluded: a synthetic in-page WAV control failed identically, proving the environment rather than the page; headless Chrome then loaded the real file at duration 17.48s
false_lead_recorded.observation: in the CDP tab the audio never left readyState 0 even from a fully fetched blob
false_lead_recorded.why_recorded: without the control this would have been filed as a page defect

note_on_scheme: served over http, not file://, because the file:// assumption was the unverified one
served_by: python3 -m http.server 8777 from the run directory
